explanation: RAII is a fundamental C++ idiom where resource management (like memory, files, network connections, locks, etc.) is tied to the object's lifetime.  Resources are acquired in the constructor and released in the destructor. This ensures resources are always cleaned up, even in the face of exceptions or premature exits, preventing resource leaks and improving program stability.  It's a cornerstone of exception safety and makes your code more robust and easier to reason about.
